record.paper_title: Some Open Problems Related to Creative Telescoping
record.original_question: Derive bounds for the bit size of telescopers for hyperexponential terms.

evidence.quote: Problem 3.2 Derive bounds for the bit size of telescopers for hyperexponential terms.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $K$ be a number field (e.g., $\mathbb{Q}$) and let $H(x,y)$ be a hyperexponential term over $K(x,y)$, that is, a nonzero function such that both logarithmic derivatives
$$\frac{\partial_x H}{H} \in K(x,y) \quad\text{and}\quad \frac{\partial_y H}{H} \in K(x,y)$$
are rational functions. A telescoper for $H$ with respect to $y$ is a nonzero linear ordinary differential operator
$$L(x,\partial_x) = \sum_{i=0}^{r} a_i(x)\, \partial_x^i, \qquad a_i(x) \in K[x],$$
for which there exists a hyperexponential certificate $G(x,y) = R(x,y)\,H(x,y)$ with $R \in K(x,y)$ such that
$$L(x,\partial_x)\,H(x,y) = \partial_y G(x,y).$$

The bit size (height) of a polynomial in $K[x]$ is the maximum number of bits required to encode its coefficients (with respect to a fixed integral basis of $K$ when $K\neq \mathbb{Q}$), and the bit size of $L$ is the maximum bit size of its coefficients $a_i(x)$ together with their degrees in $x$.

Problem. Derive explicit upper bounds on the bit size of a minimal-order telescoper $L$ for $H$, expressed in terms of structural data of $H$ (such as the degrees and bit sizes of the numerators and denominators of $\partial_x H/H$ and $\partial_y H/H$, and the order of $L$).
artifact.status_search_result: While order and degree bounds for telescopers of hyperexponential terms are known (e.g., via Hermite reduction methods and hyperbola-shaped bounds in the order-degree plane), explicit bit-size (height) bounds remain largely unaddressed. Traditional creative telescoping algorithms admit exponential bit complexity, and obtaining sharp bit-size bounds is regarded as an open problem; reduction-based approaches have made partial progress in special cases but no general bit-size bound for telescopers of hyperexponential terms appears in the literature.

status_evidence.title: Hermite Reduction and Creative Telescoping for Hyperexponential Functions
status_evidence.snippet: Hermite-like reduction for hyperexponential functions; addresses order and degree bounds but not bit size.
status_evidence.claim: Reduction-based algorithms yield order/degree bounds; bit-size bounds for hyperexponential telescopers are not provided.

status_evidence.title: Creative telescoping using reductions
status_evidence.snippet: Discusses complexity of creative telescoping and notes exponential bit complexity in traditional implementations.
status_evidence.claim: Polynomial bit complexity for creative telescoping in the general case remains open.

status_evidence.title: On the length of integers in telescopers for proper hypergeometric terms
status_evidence.snippet: Addresses integer length in telescopers for proper hypergeometric (discrete) terms, a related but distinct setting.
status_evidence.claim: Some bit-size results exist for proper hypergeometric (shift) case; hyperexponential (differential) case is less developed.
